_comment: Wave 3: engineering health. The owner asked for OOP factories where possible - script-library-refactor assesses that with evidence rather than assuming it, because ballistics-core is deliberately functional.

tasks.title: Document the script library so an agent can use it without reading source
tasks.why: scripts/ is ~50 ESM modules with five shared helpers that only 7 of them import. An agent arriving cold must rediscover which module holds what, and code-audit found 23 scripts each solving a problem scripts/shared/ already solves. Documentation is cheaper than consolidation and is what actually unblocks the next agent.
tasks.evidence: Only 7 scripts import root. The convention is documented in check-seeds.mjs and followed by 7; the other 23 each solved a problem that was already solved.
scope: Write a reference for scripts/shared/: data.mjs, encoding.mjs, bullet-sources.mjs, load-database.mjs, affiliate-links.mjs. For each export, state what it does, its exact signature, what it returns, and a one-line example. These five modules total ~54KB and are the library's entire public surface.

Build a map from task to script: for each of the ~50 scripts, one line saying what it does and what invokes it. If nothing invokes it, say so - an unreachable script is either a one-shot tool or dead code, and a reader cannot tell which.

Document the conventions a new script must follow, each with a live example: importing root from shared/data.mjs rather than deriving it, using readCsv rather than split(','), and the reason each exists. Cite the file recording the trap.
State clearly what is NOT in the library and why. The duplication that remains is deliberate in at least one case, and naming that case stops someone 'fixing' it.

Include the Windows traps, because they cost the audit three failed measurements: execFileSync with npm fails because npm is a .cmd shim, Select-String has no -Recurse, and .NET file APIs ignore PowerShell's cd so relative paths resolve to the wrong repository.
do_not: Do not write the documentation into scripts/ itself. Output stays in this folder; a human places it.
Do not refactor, rename or re-export anything. This task reads and explains.
Do not document a function you have not read. A reference that guesses is worse than none, because it will be trusted.

tasks.title: Assess script consolidation, and whether OOP factories are warranted
tasks.why: The owner asked for OOP factories where possible. That deserves a real answer rather than compliance. packages/ballistics-core is deliberately FUNCTIONAL - pure exported functions with no hidden state, and its 10 classes are reserved for things that genuinely have state (profiles, sources, devices). Blanket OOP there would be a regression dressed as progress. scripts/ is plain ESM Node, where a class wrapping a function is strictly worse than the function. So this produces the refactor that IS warranted and says plainly where a factory is not.
tasks.evidence: Measured across 50 .mjs files: 14 sites re-deriving root, 9 using process.cwd(), 9 createHash call sites, 1 reimplementing RFC 4180 CSV parsing. Only 7 scripts import root. The one that actually bites is process.cwd() rooting in 9 scripts, including check-docs.mjs.
scope: Count the duplication yourself rather than quoting the audit. Establish current numbers - the audit was a snapshot and four sites have since been fixed. A count that has drifted is worse than no count.

For each duplication class decide: consolidate into shared, or leave alone. Give the reason. The 15 re-derived roots are pure consolidation with no judgement involved; the 9 sha256 sites differ in encoding (7 hex, 2 base64) so a single helper must take the encoding as a parameter or it will be wrong for one caller.

Answer the factory question with evidence, per module. State plainly that ballistics-core's functional style is deliberate and correct for pure computation, and identify the ONE place a factory would pay: if repeated construction of a drag table or a profile object needs options validation, that is a real factory. Do not propose a factory for anything that is a pure function.

State the actual risk of consolidation. Shared helpers are load-bearing: a bug in readCsv corrupts every seed file, and code-audit already found import-bullets.mjs writing through a naive CSV split. Argue for or against centralising; do not assume it.
Produce ordered, independent change sets with exact file lists and a verification command for each, so they can be approved in batches the way the low-risk fixes were.
do_not: Do not apply any refactor. Produce the plan and the diffs.
Do not introduce classes into pure-computation modules to satisfy a general preference for OOP. That is a regression with extra indirection, and saying so is part of the deliverable.
Do not consolidate a helper whose callers differ in a way the signature does not capture. Encoding differences show up as wrong output, not as an error.

tasks.title: Adversarial review of gates, physics core, and website
tasks.why: code-audit found that a gate shipped with a missing brace, silently reduced it to checking one task per run, and reported success while four completed tasks sat unchecked - ESLint and node --check both passed. It was found by an agent doing its own task, not by a gate. That class of defect nothing currently catches, and a second pair of eyes is the cheapest mitigation available.
tasks.evidence: A gate in verify can be green and verify nothing... It was eventually found - by an agent doing its own task, not by a gate.
scope: Review scripts/gates/ adversarially, because those are the checks everything else trusts. For each, construct an input that MUST make it fail and confirm it does. A gate you cannot break is an untested gate, and saying so is the finding.

Hunt the loop-variable and scope defects code-audit documented, because they have now appeared three times in this repo: a missing closing brace silently truncating a loop, a const declared below the loop that calls it, and a gate that reads files when it should check deployed output.

Review packages/ballistics-core/src for correctness against its own doc comments, not against style. A comment describing a guarantee is a hypothesis: the CSP defect was every gate reading a file while production served no policy at all. Verify the arithmetic in densityRatio, pressureAltitudeFt and the dispersion statistics against an independent method.

Review apps/website/src for the findings ui-research recorded and did not fix: the em-dash unknown marker that reads as zero, tabular-nums absent from live fields, one accent doing two jobs, and disclosure away from the button.
Report defects with a reproduction, not a description. A finding the author cannot reproduce is an opinion.
do_not: Do not fix anything. Produce reproductions and proposed diffs.

Do not run a destructive input against the real tree. Use a throwaway copy under tmp/ - and note that a probe under tmp/ with a broken relative import measures a different module graph than the real gate, which is how a false finding gets filed.
Do not report style preferences as defects. Rank by consequence: a wrong number a user acts on, then a check that passes while verifying nothing, then everything else.

tasks.title: Audit the knowledge base for staleness and contradiction
tasks.why: Over twenty completed tasks each produced a KNOWLEDGE.md, and they contradict each other on a question that determines whether a large amount of data work is lawful. A knowledge base that silently disagrees with itself is worse than none, because a later agent will pick whichever file it read first.
tasks.evidence: No licence wall on cartridge dimensions. Every genuine gap in this task's table has a free, named, primary source... The barrier to this work is transcription effort, not permission.
scope: Inventory every KNOWLEDGE.md in tasking/completed/ and record what each claims to be authoritative about. Then find every pair that disagrees. The CIP contradiction between ammoseek-coverage and cartridge-dimensions is already known; find the others.

For each contradiction, state whether it is a genuine conflict, a difference in scope that makes both true, or one file being outdated. These need different resolutions and treating them identically wastes the reader's time.
Check claims that time has invalidated: paths that moved, counts that drifted, functions since fixed, work since done. Quote the claim and give its current state.
Propose a structure that makes contradiction VISIBLE rather than requiring a reader to hold twenty-two files in their head. State the cost of the proposal and who would maintain it.
Flag anything that, read alone, would lead an agent to do the wrong thing.
do_not: Do not resolve a contradiction by choosing a side. Record both claims with their sources; resolution is the taskmaster's or the owner's.
Do not delete or rewrite another task's KNOWLEDGE.md. This task reports; the record stays as written, because the reason a claim changed is itself worth keeping.
Do not treat an absence of contradiction as success. Twenty-two files agreeing is a claim to verify, not a fact to assume.
